name: DNS - dnsrecon Standard & Brute Force
description: Automated DNS enumeration. `-t std` runs SOA, NS, A, AAAA, MX, TXT, and SPF queries plus wildcard detection and zone transfer attempts against every NS. `-t brt` brute-forces subdomains from a wordlist.

variations.label: Reverse PTR sweep on a CIDR

notes: Run `-t std` first — if AXFR succeeds you get every record in one shot. Follow with `-t brt` against the NS servers found. Wildcard DNS (*.domain resolves to a single IP) can produce false positives in brute force; dnsrecon flags this automatically. Check MX, TXT/SPF, and NS records manually for third-party services and internal naming patterns. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 6 (Information Gathering).

attack_chain.action: Run standard enum to collect NS/MX/A/TXT records and attempt AXFR
Brute force subdomains using discovered NS server
Resolve discovered subdomains / pivot to new IPs
attack_chain.command: for sub in $(cat found_subs.txt); do host $sub; done

recommended.note: dnsenum for subdomain brute force — similar capability.
Manual dig AXFR against discovered NS servers.
Passive subdomain discovery without DNS brute force.

defense.why_it_works: dnsrecon automates systematic DNS enumeration including zone transfer attempts against every name server, wildcard detection, and record-type sweeps that manual queries miss. Zone transfers (AXFR) from misconfigured servers expose every DNS record — providing a full map of the target's infrastructure in one query.
defense.prerequisites: A target domain name; network access to DNS (UDP/TCP 53).
defense.impact: All DNS records for the zone: subdomains, internal hostnames, mail infrastructure, third-party services, and network topology hints.
defense.detection: AXFR requests from unauthorized IPs are logged by most authoritative DNS servers and should alert. High-volume A record lookups from a single IP during brute force are visible in DNS query logs.
defense.prevention: Restrict zone transfers (AXFR) to authorized secondary DNS servers only. Remove internal-only records from public-facing DNS. Enable DNS query logging and alert on AXFR attempts from unapproved sources.
